title: Gnocchi di Ricotta
subtitle: Light ricotta and Parmesan dumplings
excerpt: Gnocchi di ricotta are much lighter and faster to make than potato gnocchi: drained ricotta, Parmesan, egg, and just enough flour to bind. They are soft, pillowy, and almost melting. They take 15 minutes to mix and 2 minutes to cook. They are sometimes called malfatti (badly made) because they are shaped loosely rather than ribbed.
sourceNotes: Ricotta gnocchi (also called gnudi or malfatti in various Italian regions) are found across central and northern Italy. They are a simpler, faster alternative to potato gnocchi and are particularly associated with Tuscany and Umbria.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The dough can be made and refrigerated for up to 1 hour before shaping.

content.text: The most important step is draining the ricotta thoroughly. Wet ricotta produces sticky dough that needs too much flour to hold together, and the result is heavy. Drain in a sieve or cloth for at least 30 minutes -- an hour is better. Once the ricotta is dry, the dough comes together quickly and needs only a tablespoon or two of flour.

items.prepNote: well drained in a sieve or muslin for at least 30 minutes

content.text: Combine well-drained {{ricotta}} ricotta with {{parmesan}} Parmesan, {{eggs}} egg, {{nutmeg}} nutmeg, and {{salt-table}} salt. Add {{00-flour}} flour and mix gently until a soft, slightly sticky dough forms. Do not overwork. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Flour your hands and a board well. Shape the dough into small oval dumplings using two floured spoons or by rolling small portions gently between floured palms. Place on a floured tray.

Bring a large pan of well-salted water to a boil. Cook the gnocchi in batches until they float and have been floating for 30 seconds, about 2 to 3 minutes total. Lift with a slotted spoon straight into your sauce of choice and serve immediately.

items.symptom: The gnocchi fall apart in the water
items.cause: The ricotta was too wet or the dough had too little flour.
items.fix: Test one gnocchi first. If it breaks up, stir a little more flour into the dough and test again. Make sure the ricotta is properly drained -- this is the most common cause of failure.

content.text: Ricotta gnocchi appear across central Italy under different names: malfatti in Lombardy and Emilia, gnudi in Tuscany. The word gnudi means naked -- the filling without the pasta. They are a pasta filling (ricotta, Parmesan, egg, nutmeg) served as dumplings rather than inside pasta. They are lighter, faster, and need no pasta-making tools.
